verdict.rationale: Lium ships first-party agent-facing assets: an MCP server, llms.txt instructions written around user questions, and an official agent skill repo. Together these let a user's AI agent operate Lium from natural-language requests ("Your agent starts a pod, runs the job and removes it"). However, the natural-language interpretation is done by the external agent, and the MCP server only covers docs search and prices, not pod operations. Missing for 10: a native natural-language command interface in the product itself, MCP tools covering rent and pod management, and hands-on or independent corroboration of NL-driven operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Your agent starts a pod, runs the job and removes it, within a budget you set.
The user asks what a GPU costs to rent right now or which GPUs are available: read the public prices below, no account.
Use the MCP server at `/mcp` to search and read the docs (`search`, `read_page`) and to see live GPU prices and availability with rent links
An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
